items.title: Venezuela’s Response to Earthquakes Exposes Government’s Shortcomings
items.summary: The government turned to the world to respond to twin quakes. But years of shrinking budgets and political repression weakened its ability to rescue countless people trapped in rubble.

items.title: Fires Wrecked Their Village in France. Now They Want Answers.
items.summary: After fleeing France’s worst wildfire in decades, residents of Le Porge, a village west of Bordeaux, returned home 13 days later. They found a town in ruins.

items.title: Country Music Festival Lights Up Nairobi
items.summary: Fans gathered in Kenya to celebrate a genre born far away but that more and more Africans are coming to appreciate.

items.title: Amid Intensifying Russian Strikes, Ukraine’s Pleas for Air Defenses Are Falling Flat
items.summary: Western allies are more hesitant to give up interceptor missiles they may need for their own defense as war rages on multiple fronts.

items.title: Houthi Attacks on Yemeni Military Threaten to Reignite Civil War
items.summary: The Iranian-backed militia said it had targeted the armed forces in two resource-rich provinces, as escalating violence in Yemen imperils a fragile truce.

items.title: Israeli Settler Charged in Death of Activist Awdah Hathaleen
items.summary: The indictment was a rare case in which the Israeli authorities pressed charges against an Israeli in the killing of a Palestinian.

items.title: Driver in Munich Car Ramming Attack Given Life in Prison
items.summary: The attack, in 2025, was one of several carried out in Germany in recent years by men with migrant backgrounds, shaking the public’s sense of safety.

items.title: Can Robots Save Japan’s Aging Cherry Blossom Farmers?
items.summary: Monster Wolf and Pochi are among the robots deployed to scare away bears and transport cherry blossoms in a northern region where many farmers are in their 70s or older.

items.title: Budget Airline Jetstar to Charge Fees for Using the Overhead Bin
items.summary: Jetstar, a budget carrier, will be the first in Australia to start making passengers pay for carry-on luggage that doesn’t fit under the seat.

items.title: The ‘Heated Rivalry’ Star Hudson Williams Uplifts a Canadian Tire Bag
items.summary: After the actor Hudson Williams was photographed carrying a plaid reusable shopping bag, priced under $2, the tote has become a viral fashion accessory.

items.title: FIFA Executives Were Given Ultimatum to Approve World Cup Privatization Plan

items.title: Amid Cyclospora Outbreak, Demand for Locally Grown Lettuce Surges
items.summary: Small produce stands and farmers’ markets are seeing a surge in demand for leafy greens as sales of lettuce and salad kits from grocery chains and big retailers drop.

items.title: Drought Threatens a Vital Economic Artery in the Heart of Europe
items.summary: The Rhine conveys vessels and cargo that power European industry. Record low water levels are disrupting supply chains, adding costs and presenting fresh risks to growth.

items.title: China’s Unitree Prices IPO in Bet Investors Are Ready for Humanoid Robots
items.summary: Unitree Robotics wants to raise about $900 million in an I.P.O. that tests market interest in humanoid robots, a technology that wows but has yet to prove its viability.

items.title: What’s Behind the A.I. Shake-Up at Google
items.summary: A new role for Demis Hassabis, the head of Google’s artificial intelligence unit, reflects reality at the tech giant. Investors remain worried.

items.title: Follow the Markets and Track Stocks With These Free Apps

items.title: Why So Many C.E.O.s Are Getting a Chief of Staff
items.summary: The position as a trusted sounding board is in high demand as business gets more complex — and everyone wants to get in on the latest bureaucratic fad.

items.title: TikTok Lays Off 250 Employees in Office That Includes Content Moderation

items.title: How China’s A.I. Is Surging Across Africa
